#### Clean up

```{r}
# Make a tibble of the desired gene IDs for semi_join
genes <- tibble(Gene_ID =
                  c("Solyc07g052960",
                    "Solyc01g008710",
                    "Solyc03g111720",
                    "Solyc01g095080",
                    "Solyc05g050010",
                    "Solyc10g080210",
                    "Solyc02g036350",
                    "Solyc02g086930",
                    "Solyc02g077920",
                    "Solyc07g055920",
                    "Solyc03g114830",
                    "Solyc08g080640",
                    "Solyc05g012020",
                    "Solyc10g006880",
                    "Solyc10g047030",
                    "Solyc09g075440",
                    "Solyc03g044300",
                    "Solyc12g008840",
                    "Solyc01g009010",
                    "Solyc10g081650",
                    "Solyc09g089580",
                    "Solyc08g080090",
                    "Solyc07g049530",
                    "Solyc06g069430",
                    "Solyc04g079960",
                    "Solyc03g031860",
                    "Solyc12g098710",
                    "Solyc06g051800",
                    "Solyc01g006540",
                    "Solyc03g095900",
                    "Solyc03g083910",
                    "Solyc09g010210")
)

Data_set_1_clean <- Data_set_1 |> 
  
  # Find the first 8 columns and all coloumns of fold change
  select(matches("\\.\\.\\.[1-8]$"), starts_with("FC")) |>
  
  # Renaming coloumn names
  rename("Gene_ID" = 1,
         "Description" = 2,
         "AC_G" = 3,
         "AC_P" = 4,
         "TF18_G" = 5,
         "TF18_P" = 6,
         "rin_G" = 7,
         "rin_P" = 8,
         "FC_AC(P/G)" = 9,
         "FC_TF18(P/G)" = 10,
         "FC_rin(P/G)" = 11,
         "FC_TF18_P/AC_P" = 12,
         "FC_rin_P/AC_P" = 13,
         "FC_TF18_P/rin_P" = 14,
         "FC_TF18_G/AC_G" = 15,
         "FC_rin_G/AC_G" = 16,
         "FC_TF18_G/rin_G" = 17,
         ) |>
  
  # set Gene_ID as a factor for later plotting
  mutate(Gene_ID = as_factor(Gene_ID)) |>
  
  # Semi_join to only get the Gene_IDs used in the paper
  semi_join(genes, by = "Gene_ID") |>
  
  #Divide mean and standard deviation into each their columme
  separate_wider_delim(c(AC_G, AC_P, TF18_P, TF18_G, rin_P, rin_G),  
                       delim = " ± ",
                       names = c("mean", "sd"),
                       names_sep = "_") |>
 
   #Adding Gene_name coloumn to the end
  mutate(
    Gene_Name   = str_extract(Description, "\\(([^()]*)\\)\\s*$", group = 1),   #Finding the last parenthesis and extraction the text inside it to gene_name
    Description = str_remove(Description, "\\s*\\([^()]*\\)\\s*$")              #Removes the gene name parenthesis from the description
  ) |> 
  # manually extract the last two gene name, that are different in plots
  mutate(Gene_Name = if_else(str_detect(Description, "\\bGRAS\\b"), "GRAS", Gene_Name)) |> 
  mutate(Gene_Name = if_else(str_detect(Gene_Name, "\\bTomLoxC\\b"), "LoxC", Gene_Name)) |> 
  mutate(Gene_Name = if_else(str_detect(Gene_Name, "\\bTDR4\\b"), "FUL1<", Gene_Name))
```

## RNA-seq Data

#### Loading and inspecting file

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| warning: false

RNA_seq <- read.delim("../data/_raw/GSE49289_Fujisawa_etal_NGS_FULRNAi_RPKM.txt.gz", skip = 1, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

head(Data_set_1, 10)
```

#### Cleaning RNA-seq data

Making this data set tidy might seem a bit reversed because there are so many genes and only 9 samples. The data thereby is made extremely wide when converted into a tidy tibble. However this is needed in order to make the PCA analysis where each gene is a variable and the samples are observations. Furthermore we can in this way add the variable/coloumns of metadata of which sample we are working with (AC, TF18 or rin) and what their status where when taken (where they pink or green).

```{r}
# Making the data tidy with genes as rows and each sample as a coloumn

# Transposing the data so the variables (genes) are coloumns and observations (samples) are rows
RNA_clean <- RNA_seq |>
  rownames_to_column("gene") |>    # Making a column of genes instead of just hvaing the rownames
  pivot_longer(-gene, names_to = "sample_id", values_to = "rpkm") |> # Pivot everything but genes to longer (meaning all the samples)
  pivot_wider(names_from = gene, values_from = rpkm) |>
  separate(sample_id, sep = " ", into = c("sample", "rep")) |>
  separate(sample, sep = "-", into = c("sample", "status"))
```

## Save the workable files in data/ folder

```{r}
# use rds to save data types
write_rds(Data_set_1_clean, file = "../data/02_df1_clean.rds")
write_rds(RNA_clean, file = "../data/02_rna_clean.rds")
```
